scope: Characterize the StatusEffect opcode family for FFXIV 1.23b: dispatchers, receivers, packet shapes, data flow.
scope_notes: 1.x calls the modern 'status effect' subsystem 'SubStat'. The C++ binary has no dedicated 'StatusEffect' class hierarchy (the only StatusEffect symbol is the UI widget label s_Window_StatusEffectWidget_00fc1bec). The client receivers are named ChangeActorSubStat*/ChangeActorExtraStat*.

Four opcodes form the family: 0x0144 SetActorSubState (SubStat ModeBorder byte), 0x0145 ChangeActorExtraStat (ExtraStat / NetStat packed u32), 0x0177 SetActorStatus (single index/statusCode pair into staging array), 0x0179 SetActorStatusAll (full 20-slot status array batch).
Per the pcap-validation pass's c2sOpcodeHistogram none of these opcodes appear c2s in any of the 54 pcaps. They are all pure s2c.

0x0144.frequency_class: very_high - emitted on virtually every state change incl. zone, login, combat, gather

0x0145.frequency_class: very_high - per-bit changes of ExtraStat/NetStat fire individual packets

0x0177.frequency_class: low - single-slot status updates are rare relative to the 0x0179 batch refresh; mostly seen in party_battle_leve (26 fires)

0x0179.frequency_class: very_high - 1:1 with 0x0144/0x0145 in zone/login sequences (batch refresh on actor instantiation)

c2s_totals.note: Zero c2s emissions observed for any StatusEffect family opcode across the entire 54-pcap corpus. This is a pure s2c (server -> client) subsystem in 1.x. The c2sOpcodeHistogram dominant c2s opcodes are 0x0001 (3371), 0x00ca (16871 heartbeat), 0x012d/0x012e/0x012f/0x0133 (combat/inv/movement) - none StatusEffect family.

status_effect_data_flow_summary.no_dedicated_timer_subsystem: The 1.x client does NOT run per-effect duration countdown in C++. The client receives charaWork.statusShownTime updates via property packets (separate from this opcode family) and the Lua/Sqwt UI consumes those for countdown rendering. FUN_006EED90 is a 579-byte per-frame state-machine over a DIFFERENT 16-byte-entry list (state byte at +0xC takes values 0/2/3) reached from FUN_006FB830 / FUN_006F11B0 - likely a tick/transition driver for a parallel status queue, attribution still OPEN (an open question carried forward from the status-effect-findings pass).

Not directly invoked by the packet receivers - dispatched through the Cut::Scheduler when a sub-stat triggers a queued action.

key_findings: Four-opcode family fully bounded: 0x0144 SetActorSubState, 0x0145 ChangeActorExtraStat, 0x0177 SetActorStatus (single-slot), 0x0179 SetActorStatusAll (batch). All four route via FUN_004DC690 -> goto switchD_004dc749_caseD_f -> vftable[9] (Pattern B - actor dispatch).

Three of four opcodes have dedicated Receiver subclasses in the Lua::Script::Client::Command namespace: ChangeActorSubStatStatusReceiver (System), ChangeActorSubStatModeBorderReceiver (System), ChangeActorExtraStatReceiver (Network). 0x0177 has NO dedicated receiver - it is handled inline by the FUN_0058CCA0 third_router (BCS-Y-0404).

Catalog coverage is strong: all three receiver Apply methods, both writer paths (FUN_006FA980 ExtraStat merge, FUN_006EECB0 ModeBorder, FUN_00707D60 statusArray), the lazy storage allocator (FUN_006EEC00), and eight N-API facet readers are catalogued from the receiver-apply-findings and status-effect-findings passes. Only documentation gap: the 0x0177 case body inside FUN_0058CCA0.

No 'StatusEffect' C++ class exists in 1.x. The only StatusEffect symbol is s_Window_StatusEffectWidget UI label. 1.x uses 'SubStat' for what modern FFXIV calls status effects, plus 'ExtraStat' / 'NetStat' for the packed-bit ancillary state.

All four opcodes are pure s2c: c2sOpcodeHistogram across 54 pcaps shows zero c2s emissions for any of them. Status effect mutation is server-authoritative and the client is a passive applier with Lua callback fan-out per changed field.

Per-bit Lua callback fan-out is the architectural distinguisher: FUN_006FA980 (0x0145 writer) is an atomic merge-write that fires _onChangeNetStatUser / _onChangeNetStatSystem ONLY for bits that actually changed. This is a deliberate optimization to avoid spurious Lua UI rebinding.

Status timers (charaWork.statusShownTime) are NOT delivered via this opcode family - they flow through a separate ActorPropertyPacketUtil property-packet stream (likely 0x0137 SetActorProperty), with the client running NO C++ countdown logic.

FUN_006EED90 (579-byte per-frame state machine over 16-byte-entry list with state byte at +0xC taking values 0/2/3) remains UNATTRIBUTED to a specific opcode/class - carried forward from status_effect_findings.json as an open question. Could be the status-effect tick driver for the staging array path.
open_questions_carried: FUN_006EED90 per-frame iterator: which subsystem owns it? (open per the status-effect-findings pass)
The eight sub_stat_enum integer constants (Status / Mode / Waste / Guard / Chant / Object / Breakage / MotionPack) have no enumerated numeric values yet - likely Lua-side enum table.
0x0177 single-slot staging array's relationship to CharaSubStatStorage.statusArray: are they the same data structure (read/write via different paths) or two parallel structures?

The 'Network::ChangeActorExtraStatReceiver' namespace contrasts with the 'System::ChangeActorSubStat*Receiver' namespace. Why is ExtraStat in Network but the SubStat siblings in System? Possible historical split when ExtraStat was extracted from the network-derived auto-update path.
